comments.body: Oo this may be a much simpler repro than #2252 (which I spent some time digging through but was too complex to isolate). I'll take a look.

I tried to poke around. And here is what I found so far: we get an initial refcount = 1 for these inputs when parsing inputs and build variant list. Then we +1 to the refcount when entering the function in vm. And then when calling into `hal.buffer_view.buffer` the refcount for `%arg` was decreased by 1 in a non-trivial (in the sense of code layering) way: it's via `DispatchFunctor::ApplyFn`'s heavy templating. But `%arg0`'s refcount remains as 2 until the program exit and then it gets decreased to 1 by variant list free. So it still lingers on..
I *feel* we might missing refcount clean up when leaving a vm function? But I'm not very efficient when parsing through the vm layers. ;)

I suspect it's staying alive in the stack somehow. For the buffer that is correctly freed the ApplyFn is doing a move (transferring ownership) and then release when the ApplyFn returns, hence the 2->1. I have some nice debug logging for the C++ ref_ptr type https://github.com/google/iree/blob/4e4f587b254c7e12aa3ceddb121a7cd54d4d1f83/iree/base/ref_ptr.h#L29 that I need to add in for the vm type.

But should `ApplyFn` use move semantics? The `%arg1` view can potentially be used by another call following the existing `vm.call @hal.buffer_view.buffer`? I *feel* it should not change refcount at all and let the vm function exit to decrease? At the moment because `vm.call @hal.buffer_view.buffer` only takes in `%arg1` so `%arg0` is entirely left where with its original refcount = 2 after entering `@main$sync`. 

(But OTOH, I doubt we haven't hit the case that multiple uses of the same input view and don't know how that managed to not blow up thus far. ;-P)

whether to use a move or not is determined by the compiler:
https://github.com/google/iree/blob/4c0a53e955c44480e2387a9d756a33f66830a394/iree/vm/module_abi_packing.h#L209-L214
the register allocator knows if a value is the last use and will add the MOVE bit - just like a C++ programmer would add std::move of a shared_ptr vs copying it and increasing the ref count.
Ooooh, of course, compilers to the rescue. :) :) :)  Very cool stuff! :D :D :D Eager to chat more.

I think I found the issue. For some reason I added a "leak this ref" line:
https://github.com/google/iree/blob/b39149801a2c0dafaab23c06137db64962242745/iree/vm/module_abi_packing.h#L424

This would overwrite results from cross-module calls (like HAL calls) in cases where one or more registers were unused (or last-used) by the cross-module call. Will do a bit more verification and try #2252 as it should fix that too!

issue.body:
At the moment IREE runtime is leaking buffers allocated for unused inputs. A repro case:

```mlir
func @main(%arg0: tensor<4xf32>, %arg1: tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xf32> attributes {iree.module.export} {
  return %arg1 : tensor<4xf32>
}
```

```shell
$ iree-translate -iree-mlir-to-vm-bytecode-module --iree-hal-target-backends=vulkan-spirv ../unused-input.mlir > unused-input.vmfb 

$ iree-run-module --input_file=unused-input-vmla.vmfb --entry_function=main --inputs="4xf32,4xf32" --driver=vulkan

F ../third_party/vulkan_memory_allocator/src/vk_mem_alloc.h:11175] Check failed: m_pMetadata->IsEmpty() && "Some allocations were not freed before destruction of this memory block!"
```

This is made obvious by Vulkan's VMA allocator. But it's not specific to Vulkan HAL backend; the code in the above does not perform any computation at all. It should also be revealed via ASAN for other backends.
